{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -V
#   -N prism
#   -q exclusive
#   -A etc
#   -l select=1:ncpus=68:mpiprocs=24:ompthreads=1
#   -l walltime=04:00:00
#   -m abe
#   -M sylee2519@naver.com
#   -W sandbox=PRIVATE

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 24 \
  -c 1 \
  --time=4h \
  --queue=exclusive \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS -A etc (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: PBS -V (export all environment variables) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: if your Flux submission environment does not already propagate needed variables,
# the job may behave differently.

# NOTE: PBS -m/-M email notifications have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive abort/begin/end emails.

# NOTE: PBS -W sandbox=PRIVATE has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: if sandboxing affects filesystem isolation/performance on your system,
# behavior and I/O performance may differ.

# NOTE: PBS select requested ncpus=68. We request 24 tasks (-n 24) to match mpiprocs=24 and c=1 to match ompthreads=1,
# but we do not explicitly request the remaining (68-24) cores.
# Performance implication: if the application actually expects access to all 68 cores (or uses them indirectly),
# it may run slower due to fewer allocated CPU resources.

# NOTE: PBS job name (-N prism) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

cd "${PBS_O_WORKDIR:-$PWD}"

module purge
module load craype-x86-skylake gcc/7.2.0 openmpi/3.1.0
module load forge/18.1.2
module load cmake/3.17.4
module load python/3.7
module load tensorflow/1.12.0

python test2.py 1>stdout 2>stderr
'
"
}
